newsitem.title: CHINA: China's farmers to spend more on production in '97.
newsitem.headline: China's farmers to spend more on production in '97.

text.p: China's farmers will pour more money into production in 1997, including investment in fixed assets and materials used for agricultural production, the China Business Times said on Thursday.
The average investment in production by individual farmers would reach 830.8 yuan in 1997, up 11.1 percent from 1996, it said, quoting a nation-wide survey.
Investment in fixed assets, such as tractors and other farm machinery, was forecast to rise in 1997, it said.
Investment in large tractors would increase 10.7 percent from a year ago while spending on small tractors would rise 9.3 percent, the newspaper said.

Spending on diesel oil for farm use would rise 19.8 percent in 1997 year-on-year, while investment in pesticides, fertilisers and other agricultural production materials would also increase at differing rates, it said.
China's central and western areas would record sharper increases in investment by individual farmers this year than the eastern part of the country, the newspaper said.
